notes:
Written by am-06-x from three pages (budget 2-5). Not settled:
(1) The infobox/lead span is 1541-1818; the dossier runs to 1826 because the royalist south (Concepcion region to 1822, Valdivia to 1820, Chiloe to 1826) was still Spanish land. The page gives no area, no Atacama or Copiapo boundary, no southern limit; its 'southern parts of Argentina in the Patagonia region' and the 21.5 S northern limit of 1793 are not drawn. The Cliopatria Spanish Empire shape inside Chile (reaching 42.8 S from 1600) contradicts the Arauco War page and was used only up to the Maule-Bio-Bio line; the drawn south is discs around the cities.
(2) Dates not on the pages: Valdivia's death (Tucapel), the Treaties of Quillin (1641) and Negrete (1726), Valdivia's recapture year, Chacabuco's neighbour battles; the founding years of the southern cities and of the Chiloe settlement (confidence 1 event at 1550 for them and Cuyo). The Real Audiencia (1565-1573, 1606) and the 1778 captaincy-general rank are not on the Chile page (the Peru page says a Bourbon captaincy general was made in 1789 and Chile was 'segregated from the Viceroyalty on 1798').
(3) Counterpart 'mapuche' needs a dossier (am-06-b also suggested it); the Mapuche held the land south of the Bio-Bio until the 'Occupation of Araucania' (1861-1883) and Tapihue 1825 (not on the pages). 'republic-of-chile' is the Cliopatria row (1812-2024, group am-08), which starts with the Patria Vieja shape (226,000 km2) and has no row for 1815-1819.
(4) The page says Cuyo was transferred in 1776 and the Rio de la Plata dossier lists it as a gain; the Rio de la Plata page itself says only that the king gave Cevallos 'the corregimiento of Cuyo'. The Valdivia re-establishment of 1645 is the researcher's reading of the infobox span.
